analysis: Synovial fluid from patients with gout often contains urate crystals, specifically monosodium urate crystals. These crystals precipitate in joints due to high levels of uric acid and are a hallmark of gouty arthritis. While other crystals like calcium oxalate or triple phosphate can be present in synovial fluid in different conditions, the presence of urate crystals is most strongly associated with gout.
